topics.title: UN report spotlights everyday chemicals
topics.summary: A new UN report says chemicals that can affect hormones, found in many everyday products, pose a growing health and environmental concern as research improves understanding of their effects.
topics.discussionPrompt: When you hear that ordinary products have hidden trade-offs, do you become a label-reader, look for simpler options, or decide life is already complicated enough?

topics.title: Leaders gather for Asia talks
topics.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines for meetings with Southeast Asian leaders before planned talks in China involving China and Russia.
topics.discussionPrompt: At a big international gathering, what sounds more productive: the official speeches, a quiet side meeting, or the shared meal afterward?

topics.title: AI chip access rules tighten
topics.summary: The U.S. issued rules aimed at limiting remote access to advanced American chips and servers, adding another chapter to the global debate over powerful AI technology.
topics.discussionPrompt: If powerful technology needs guardrails, should the first focus be access, safety testing, or clear accountability when things go wrong?

topics.title: Nvidia earnings draw market attention
topics.summary: Technology shares have been unsettled ahead of Nvidia's results, as investors weigh chip restrictions, AI spending, and whether the sector's rapid growth can continue.
topics.discussionPrompt: When everyone watches one company for clues about a whole trend, does that feel sensible, overdramatic, or a little of both?

topics.title: Nike maps a performance-led plan
topics.summary: Nike said it expects core performance sports to drive much of its planned revenue growth through 2031, emphasizing its push to reconnect with athletes and sports fans.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a brand feel genuinely connected to a sport: great gear, memorable athletes, local community support, or something else?

topics.title: Disney plans more content spending
topics.summary: Disney reported quarterly results above Wall Street expectations, helped by theme-park attendance and NFL viewership, and said it plans to raise content spending in its next fiscal year.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you had a bigger entertainment budget, would you spend it on a spectacular new show, live events, parks, or better ways to find hidden gems?

topics.title: Retirement-plan enrollment rules arrive
topics.summary: The U.S. Treasury and IRS issued final rules for automatic enrollment in certain workplace retirement plans, carrying out provisions of a 2022 law.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would automatic saving make your future self happier, or would you rather make every money decision manually?

topics.title: Federal Reserve discusses digital finance
topics.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank will work with the private sector on responsible financial innovation while traditional payment systems remain important.
topics.discussionPrompt: What payment method feels most futuristic to you: tapping a phone, instant transfers, digital wallets, or simply never carrying cash?

topics.title: Las Vegas opens a huge flower show
topics.summary: Bellagio's annual holiday flower display opened with roughly 20,000 plants and up to 150 varieties, turning its conservatory into a seasonal attraction for visitors.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could design a giant seasonal display, would you choose flowers, lights, food, music, or a totally strange theme?

topics.title: Data centers raise climate questions
topics.summary: A Harvard study found that the 400 largest U.S. data centers emitted more heat-trapping gas in one year than Denmark, before the recent AI-driven expansion accelerated.
topics.discussionPrompt: When technology gets more useful but uses more energy, what would you most want improved first: efficiency, clean power, or less wasteful habits?
